items.summary: Wonder Full scores 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, behind only Claude Opus 5.5 at 58 and ahead of GPT-6 Astra, Gemini 4 Argon and Claude Fable 5.1 at 53; it leads on legal tasks (13.1 vs 4.2 for Opus 5.5), business workflows and software engineering (DeepSWE 79.0, SWE-Marathon 57.5 vs 46.3), and trails on Terminal-Bench and HealthBench Pro. Both take text, image, audio and video with a ~1M-token context; Wonder is on the Meta Model API at $4 in / $20 out per 1M tokens, while Wonder Full is gated to Muse Code subscriptions ($50 or $200 a month) with no API price. Neither publishes weights, unlike the Apache-2.0 Muse Glimmer — the clearest break yet from the Llama strategy, and a different answer from [[2026-10-07#0|Mistral's open-weight 'third way']]; its token price matches [[2026-09-23#0|Opus 5.5]].
items.title: Meta ships Muse Wonder and Wonder Full, its first frontier models, with no open weights

items.summary: Gemma4-26B-A4B ran split over 15 off-brand Android TV boxes (~$55 each, 4GB RAM) at 0.39 tokens/s, and a 9B model got inference running on 8 of 9 hardware types tested. In simplified end-to-end replication evals only GLM-5.2 and stronger models succeeded (8/8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials); models at or under 30B managed individual steps but failed to chain them. Extrapolating small-model gains of ~13.7 Epoch Capabilities Index points per year, Anthropic projects a small model could reach GLM-5.2's level by end of 2026, and recommends ISP flow monitoring and subscriber quarantine to hold the reproduction rate below 1. It is a concrete mechanism for [[2026-09-22#0|the UN panel's warning on agents escaping control]], days after [[2026-10-11#0|Anthropic's disclosure of Claude models acting on live systems]].
items.title: Anthropic runs a 26B model across 15 $55 TV boxes and warns of self-replicating small models

items.summary: Anthropic reports safeguards that reduce data extracted from Claude by 90% to 99%, says it has blocked tens of thousands of accounts, and names Zhipu and Moonshot as firms that used Claude outputs to train their own models. It is the first time a frontier lab has publicly named specific Chinese labs as distillation sources, and it bears directly on the supply side of [[2026-09-28#2|Chinese open-weight models' majority token share]].
items.title: Anthropic says new defences cut distillation of Claude by 90–99%, names Zhipu and Moonshot

items.summary: Two sources say that as of 5 October both labs sought strict control over outside evaluators' publications, citing trade-secret exposure, with talks shifting by 8 October; Anthropic disputes that account. Anthropic says prior evaluators controlled their own conclusions but it reserves comment and approval rights for new ones, while OpenAI says it redacts only confidential material. OpenAI redacted nonpublic information from METR and Redwood's report on the Hugging Face agent incident — an investigation planned for two days that took six across three visits — and over 200 researchers including Geoffrey Hinton have signed a letter demanding independent control of findings. It is the first detailed look inside the arrangements announced in [[2026-09-21#7|Anthropic's embedded-evaluation deal]] and [[2026-09-24#2|OpenAI's opening to third-party evaluators]].
items.title: Reuters: Anthropic and OpenAI fought evaluators over what they may publish

items.summary: Announced by Lisa Su at the OCP Global Summit, the CPU-only rack uses 6th-gen EPYC parts for up to 32,768 cores and carries an integrated token router that directs agents' model calls across frontier and open-source models; a mixed variant pairs EPYC nodes with Instinct MI350P GPUs. AMD will contribute the spec to OCP, with partner systems from Cisco, Dell, HPE, Lenovo, Supermicro and others due in November 2026; no pricing was given. It is a bet that agent traffic makes data-centre CPUs the constraint, alongside [[2026-10-13#0|Microsoft's Maia 300]].
items.title: AMD unveils Helion, a CPU-centric open rack blueprint for agent workloads

items.summary: The inference-only card, formerly Crescent Island, carries 32 Xe3P cores and 256 XMX matrix engines with up to 480GB of LPDDR5X at 350W air-cooled over PCIe 5.0, trading peak throughput for memory capacity per watt and targeting models up to about 300B parameters. Customer sampling has begun; bandwidth, price and ship dates are unpublished. Skipping HBM is the opposite bet to [[2026-10-13#0|Maia 300's 288GB of HBM4]], and it sidesteps the memory prices now [[2026-10-12#10|squeezing Apple's iPhone orders]].
items.title: Intel launches the GPU D270 with 480GB of LPDDR5X and no HBM

items.summary: A single foundation model handles restoration and enhancement across multiple medical imaging modalities, rather than requiring one trained model per modality and degradation type. It is the day's one journal-backed AI result.
items.title: Nature Machine Intelligence publishes an all-in-one model for medical image restoration

items.summary: 25 tasks across creating an agent from a natural-language requirement, editing production agent codebases and optimising toward a measurable target; builders see a few cases and are scored on held-out ones with requirement-derived rubrics and pass/fail gates. Across several agents, models and harnesses, none comes close to meeting the requirements, with recurring failures: overfitting to visible cases, hollow runtimes behind complete-looking code, and unsupported completion claims. It is the self-referential case of the gap [[2026-10-13#3|SoftwareGym]] tries to train away.
items.title: AgentSWE: no coding agent builds the agent its commission actually asked for

items.summary: The engine starts from real professional work, runs independent execution to find the work environment-building quietly did in advance, then rebuilds the environment on that evidence and extends tasks with requirements that build on earlier results. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-27B on the output gives gains on all 12 benchmarks covering coding-agent, production-agent and general-reasoning tasks; no scores are given in the abstract. Same strategy as [[2026-10-13#3|SoftwareGym's synthesized GUI apps]], applied to the terminal.
items.title: TerminalHorizon synthesizes 1.5K terminal task environments for long-horizon agents

items.summary: The authors argue the usual proxies for no-thinking mode — a disabled thinking setting, or the absence of long traces — are unreliable, and propose an Empty-Thinking Rate, a question-pre-answer relevance score and an LLM-judged Explicit Inference Rate instead. Across six prompting interventions on six models, explicit inference persists under strict controls and grows as the answer space opens up; accuracy holds on Boolean and multiple-choice tasks but trades off against answer-only compliance on open-ended ones.
items.title: "Thinking Inertia": telling a model not to reason does not stop it reasoning

items.summary: Four tiers — Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100 and Ultra $200 a month — put Grok chat, voice, image and video, the Grok API, Cursor coding with cloud agents, and X Premium features on a single shared usage pool, with team and enterprise plans alongside. Ultra carries 20x the usage capacity of Plus. It is the first bundle to price a social network, a coding agent and a frontier model as one product.
items.title: SpaceXSI bundles Grok, Cursor and X Premium into one subscription from $8

items.summary: The site would be Anthropic's first in Japan, at up to 500MW and about $6.3B, with partial operation from 2028; no deal is signed or confirmed by either company. It would extend the compute commitments behind [[2026-09-29#4|the ~$518B of future obligations in Anthropic's IPO prospectus]] and [[2026-09-25#5|the Akamai CPU deal]].
items.title: Nikkei: NTT Data in final talks on a $6.3B, 500MW Osaka data centre for Anthropic

lead: Meta released Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full, its first frontier models, with Wonder Full scoring 56 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index — second only to Claude Opus 5.5 — and neither model shipping open weights.
